note.explanation: Artificial propagation is when people grow new plants using parts of a plant, such as stems or roots. Cutting and grafting are two common methods. These methods can preserve useful characteristics, but the new plants have little genetic variation.
examples: Roses and grapevines can be grown from stem cuttings.
Sweet potato can be grown from root cuttings.
note.checkAnswer: Cutting uses a cut piece of stem or root to grow a new plant. Grafting joins plant parts so they grow as one plant.
note.simple: People can make new plants from plant parts instead of seeds. A piece can be planted, or parts of two plants can be joined.
note.checkQuestion: What is one difference between cutting and grafting?
note.title: Growing plants from plant parts
steps: For cutting, cut a piece of stem or root from a plant and use it to grow a new plant.
For grafting, attach a bud or small stem of one plant to the roots or stems of a second plant.
Remember that grafting can combine beneficial characteristics of two plants.
Remember that vegetative propagation produces plants identical to the parent, so they share the same strengths and weaknesses.
note.answer: Cutting grows a new plant from a cut piece of stem or root; grafting joins a bud or small stem of one plant to the roots or stems of another plant.

written.text: Describe the advantages and disadvantages of vegetative propagation.
written.finalAnswer: It produces many new plants in a short time, and the plants are identical to the parent and retain its useful characteristics. However, they have no genetic differences, so they may be equally sensitive to environmental changes and prone to the same diseases or pests.

written.text: How do asexual and sexual reproduction contribute differently to genetic diversity of plant populations?
written.finalAnswer: Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction and produces offspring identical to the parent, so it does not create genetic differences among them. Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from gametes and can produce variation among offspring.

explain.title: Artificial propagation
explain.body: Artificial propagation includes the methods in which humans produce new plants by using the vegetative parts of plants. The section names cutting, grafting and tissue culture as techniques.

explain.title: Cutting
explain.body: In some plants, a piece of stem or root can grow into a new plant. Roses and grapevines are examples of stem cuttings, while sweet potato is an example of a root cutting.

explain.title: Grafting
explain.body: Grafting joins a bud or small stem of one plant to the roots or stems of a second plant. It can combine beneficial characteristics of two plants and is used for many commercial fruit trees and ornamental plants.

explain.title: Advantages and disadvantage
explain.body: Vegetative propagation can produce many plants quickly and keeps useful characteristics because the new plants are like the parent. But the offspring have no genetic differences, so they may share sensitivity to environmental changes and the same diseases or pests.

mistakes: Do not define cutting as joining two plants; joining plant parts describes grafting.
Do not say grafting uses a whole seed. It joins a bud or small stem to the roots or stems of another plant.
Do not give only benefits when asked for advantages and disadvantages; include the lack of genetic differences and shared vulnerability.
Do not confuse stem cuttings with root cuttings: roses and grapevines are stem-cutting examples, while sweet potato is a root-cutting example.
Do not say vegetative offspring have genetic differences; the section states they are identical.
